CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain at the end of right middle finger.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
41-year-old female presents with right middle finger pain that began 4-5 days ago following a motor vehicle accident. Patient was stopped at a four-way stop when she was rear-ended by another vehicle. She became angry at the other driver and attempted to make an obscene gesture, but struck the ceiling of her car instead, injuring her right middle finger. The other vehicle had minimal damage (crumpled trunk). X-ray shows a distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Physical examination reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger with normal examination otherwise.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation.

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over the distal phalanx of the right middle finger. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger shows distal phalanx fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. Patient to be placed in finger splint. Prescribed tramadol 50 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain, dispensed 8 tablets. Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks.
